overview.title: What a water inspection actually is
overview.body: It's a non-destructive check-up for your home, done with two instruments: a thermal camera that reads surface temperature to spot hidden moisture, and a moisture meter that confirms and measures it - no drilling, no broken tiles.

terms.title: Leakage
terms.body: Water actively coming from a broken pipe, a failed joint, or a crack - usually the most urgent, since it's a live source.

terms.title: Seepage
terms.body: Water slowly passing through porous concrete or weak waterproofing - most often from a bathroom, terrace, or the flat above.

terms.title: Dampness
terms.body: Moisture that has settled into a wall or floor and isn't drying out - the visible result of leakage, seepage or condensation.

tools.title: The thermal camera
tools.body: Wet material loses heat differently from dry material, so moisture shows up as a distinct patch on camera - often weeks before a stain is visible to the eye.

tools.title: The moisture meter
tools.body: Pinless meters glide over a surface to read moisture underneath without touching it. Pin meters confirm the exact figure at one spot. We use both to be sure.

why.title: Water is the most expensive problem a home can hide
paragraphs: By the time a stain appears on your ceiling, moisture has usually been travelling inside the structure for months - quietly damaging plaster, wiring conduits and the slab itself.
Proofit traces it to the true source - bathrooms, terraces, external walls, concealed plumbing - non-destructively, with thermal and photographic evidence for every finding.

process.title: How the inspection runs
process.lede: Four steps, in this order, on a single visit.

steps.title: Thermal survey
steps.body: A full scan of the affected area and every adjoining wall, ceiling or floor it touches.

steps.title: Moisture mapping
steps.body: Readings across flagged zones, to separate an active leak from an old, drying stain.

steps.title: Source tracing
steps.body: Root-cause analysis - concealed plumbing, waterproofing failure, ingress, or condensation.

steps.title: Evidence report
steps.body: Thermal- and photo-documented, with severity grading and rectification guidance.

faqs.q: Will this damage my walls or tiles?
faqs.a: No. The pin-type meter leaves two tiny needle marks, invisible once painted over - nothing else is drilled, cut or opened.

faqs.q: How long does it take, and how soon do I get the report?
faqs.a: Usually half a day on-site depending on property size, with the report delivered 2-5 business working days after the visit.

faqs.q: Can I use this report with my builder or society?
faqs.a: Yes. Because Proofit is independent of any builder, developer or society, the report is neutral, evidence-backed documentation you can present to whoever needs to act on it.

faqs.q: What's the difference between this and a full Home Inspection?
faqs.a: Water Inspection focuses specifically on leakage, seepage and dampness. Home Inspection is broader and also covers civil finishes, electrical, doors, windows and fittings - book Water Inspection on its own when water is your only concern.

faqs.q: Worth doing before the monsoon even with no visible problem?
faqs.a: Yes - that's when it's most useful. Most seepage starts invisibly, and catching it before the monsoon is far cheaper than repairing water damage after it.

overview.title: What a home inspection actually is
overview.body: It's a structured, room-by-room check-up of everything in your flat - civil finishes, electrical, plumbing, doors and windows, waterproofing, fittings - against a checklist, so defects are documented while there's still someone accountable to fix them.

terms.title: Snag
terms.body: A defect or incomplete item - a chipped tile, a misaligned door, a switch that doesn't work - flagged before you take ownership.

terms.title: Checklist audit
terms.body: A structured walkthrough against an international-standard checklist, adapted to Indian apartment construction, so nothing is left to memory.

terms.title: Rectification
terms.body: The builder or contractor fixing flagged snags, verified again before you sign off on possession or release final payment.

tools.title: Structured on-site evaluation
tools.body: Every room, surface and system checked against the same checklist, so the result depends on the property - not on which inspector shows up.

tools.title: Thermal imaging cross-check
tools.body: Wet areas and electrical points get an added thermal pass, catching hidden dampness or hot-spots the eye alone would miss - without opening anything up.

why.title: A flat that looks finished isn't necessarily built right
paragraphs: Our inspectors evaluate every room, surface and system against a structured checklist adapted to Indian construction and apartment layouts - not a quick walkthrough.
Each inspection combines expert on-site evaluation with thermal imaging, and concludes with a detailed, photo-backed snag report - so builders rectify before you sign, and you negotiate with facts.
